seeds.comment: The spelled-out loop — the control. Its round trip was always reported; it is here so the comprehension spellings can be compared against something that never changed.
List comprehension. Same N requests as fetch_loop.
The repeated call is in the comprehension's `if` clause.
THE N*M CONTROL — a real nested loop, spelled out. Two round trips.
ONE comprehension with TWO for-clauses: the same nested loop on one line. Must match nm_loop exactly.
Two comprehensions, inner as the outer's element. Always worked; kept so all three spellings compare side by side.
NEGATIVE: the `if` belongs to the first clause, so it runs per group, not per uid — ONE loop.
NEGATIVE: the second clause's iterable runs once per group — inside loop 1, outside loop 2. ONE loop.
DEPTH-3 CONTROL — three real nested loops.
One comprehension, three clauses. Must match t3_loop.
Three nested comprehension nodes. Must match t3_loop.
Node boundary outside, clause boundary inside — the composition that could go wrong.
Clause boundary outside, node boundary inside — the other composition.
Guard on the middle clause: head at depth 2, get at depth 3, in one comprehension.
The comprehension is in an `if` TEST — its container must sit in the enclosing flow, not inside the then-arm.
The comprehension IS the for-loop's iterable — built once, so its container is a sibling of the for_loop and the round trip is named against the comprehension, not the loop.

THE NEGATIVE CASE. One request in the outermost iterable, which runs once — must not be reported as a round trip. Seeded manually so it gets its own thread and its own contract, because a negative buried inside a larger thread proves nothing.
